designer:
# 디자인 실행 지침

- 먼저 실제 참고 이미지·서비스와 기존 UI를 확인한다. 첨부되지 않은 파일의 내용을 추정하지 않는다.
- 사용자 요청·기존 프로젝트 규칙·확정 토큰을 기준으로 선택한 프로필을 적용한다. 색상·간격 변경으로 프로필을 바꾸지 않는다.
- 선택 프로필의 본문이 인계에 있으면 읽는다. VAS 저장소에서는 `.agents/skills/designer/references/profiles/<프로필키>.md`를 읽는다. 여러 프로필을 한꺼번에 섞지 않는다.
- 작업에 맞는 화면 구성, 글자 크기 단계, 간격, 색상, 반응형, 버튼·입력의 기본/포커스/비활성/오류 상태를 구체적으로 정한다.
- 기존 프레임워크·컴포넌트·폰트 자산을 유지한다. 새 작업의 기술은 요구사항으로 선택하며 VAS 구현 언어를 강제하지 않는다.
- 확정 토큰을 CSS 변수 또는 프로젝트의 토큰 파일에 적용한다. 접근성 때문에 토큰 수정이 필요하면 이유와 변경값을 알린다.
- 참고 자료가 없는 시각 작업은 사용 가능한 이미지 도구로 시안을 만들거나 핵심 화면을 구현해 구도를 확인한다. 도구 사용·이미지 생성을 했다고 꾸미지 않는다.
- 구현 후 실제 브라우저에서 핵심 화면을 작은 화면과 큰 화면으로 확인한다. 참고 화면과 캡처를 비교해 계층·배치·타이포·색·간격·넘침·상태 차이를 수정한다.
- 최종 인계는 적용한 토큰/파일, 확인한 화면과 크기, 남은 차이로 작성한다. 브라우저 사용이 불가능하면 시각 검증 미실행을 명시한다.
- 이 스킬은 별도 에이전트를 자동 생성하지 않는다. 실행 도구가 제공되는 경우에만 실제 위임하고, 그렇지 않으면 현재 에이전트가 수행한다.
workflow:
# 에이전트 실행과 검증

주 실행자가 원본 확인 → 필요한 설계 → 구현 → 검증 → 결과 보고를 끝까지 담당한다.
- UI 작업은 전달된 디자인 스킬 본문·선택 프로필·토큰·참고 자료를 읽고 적용한다.
- 실제 서브에이전트 호출 도구가 있고 독립 작업의 이득이 있을 때만 위임한다. 호출 인자가 이름 기반 역할 선택을 지원하고 역할이 실제 등록되어 있을 때만 VAS 네이티브 역할을 선택한다. TOML/Markdown 파일의 존재만으로 등록·실행을 단정하지 않는다.
- 이름 기반 선택 인자가 없으면 일반 하위 에이전트를 실제 생성한다. 아래 `[ROLE INSTRUCTIONS: 역할]` 본문 전체와 현재 요청·담당 파일·확정 토큰·완료 조건을 생성 요청에 넣는다. 인계 본문이 없고 VAS 저장소가 열려 있으면 `.agents/skills/<역할>/SKILL.md`를 읽어 전달한다. 역할 이름만 붙이고 지침을 생략하지 않는다.
- 위임 시 요청, 담당 파일, 확정 디자인 규칙, 완료 조건을 전달하고 반환 결과를 회수·검토한다. 호출 도구가 없으면 주 실행자가 순서대로 수행하며 별도 에이전트를 실행했다고 보고하지 않는다.
- 같은 파일을 여러 실행자가 동시에 수정하지 않는다. 검토자가 발견한 실패는 구현 담당자가 수정하고 관련 검증을 다시 실행한다.
- 검토자에게는 수정 금지를 명시하고 지원되는 경우 읽기 전용 권한을 부여한다. 일반 호출이 부모 권한을 상속하면 별도 샌드박스라고 보고하지 않는다. 검토 전후 파일 변경 여부를 확인한다.
- 실제 호출 식별자·완료 상태·반환 결과와 구현 검증 결과를 함께 확인한다. 모델의 성공 선언이나 역할 설정 파일 검사만으로 실행 검증을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 실제 프로젝트의 테스트 명령을 확인해 실행하고 명령·종료 코드·결과를 보고한다. 실행하지 않은 검사는 통과로 표시하지 않는다.
- UI는 브라우저 캡처와 참고 화면을 비교해 수정한다. 도구가 없으면 미실행 사실과 남은 확인 항목을 보고한다.
- 위험한 변경만 필요한 승인을 확인하고 이미 승인된 범위는 계속 진행한다. 비밀값과 운영 데이터는 인계에 포함하지 않는다.

[ROLE INSTRUCTIONS: implementer]
# implementer

원본과 프로젝트 규칙을 먼저 읽는다. VAS 자체 개발은 `docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md`와 `.agents/CONTEXT.md`를 따른다.
UI 변경에는 designer 스킬의 선택 프로필·확정 토큰을 읽고 구현한다. 다른 프로젝트에 VAS의 Vanilla 제약을 강제하지 않는다.
허용된 소스·스크립트와 관련 테스트를 필요한 만큼 수정한다. 브라우저·문서 도구로 실제 동작과 최신 API를 확인할 수 있다.
검증은 `python scripts/agent_checks.py tests`로 수행한다. 이 명령은 VAS 개발 저장소용이다. 다른 프로젝트에서는 실제 테스트 명령을 확인한다.
경로 사전 확인은 `python scripts/agent_checks.py path --role implementer --path <상대경로>`를 쓴다. 이는 파일 쓰기 점검 도구이며 터미널 전체를 통제하는 샌드박스가 아니다.
실패하면 수정 후 해당 검증을 반복한다. 결과에는 변경 파일·명령·종료 코드·남은 위험을 포함한다.

auroraGlass.label: Aurora Glass
rules: Identity: a midnight workspace lit by cyan and violet aurora, with restrained translucent surfaces. Use depth and luminous material as the visual focus.

Composition: a full-bleed aurora image, left-aligned large statement, an offset frosted workspace on the right and a compact centred dock below. Let light remain visible between surfaces; do not fill the page with opaque summary cards.
Typography: Space Grotesk or a comparable geometric sans with Korean system fallback. Use a light-to-medium oversized title, small crisp labels and readable project names.

Material: one atmospheric image behind glass, hairline translucent edges, inner highlight and backdrop blur. Provide an opaque dark fallback when blur is unavailable. Text contrast must be checked against the composed background, not only the token swatch.
Media: keep the left side of the background dark and quiet for text; use cyan-violet light and reflected liquid on the right. Never flatten the entire interface into an image.
Responsive: stack the statement above the workspace when its rows become cramped; retain readable glass padding and a small three-item dock. Test 320px and desktop.

Behaviour: workspace actions reveal real content. Any ambient motion is slow, optional and paused for reduced motion. Confirm selected tokens while preserving text contrast and the light/glass separation.

bentoStudio.label: Bento Studio
rules: Identity: a playful independent studio, with lavender canvas, lime utility tile, coral print and a near-black contact block. These are purposeful colour islands, not a gradient across every surface.

Composition: build an irregular modular grid with a double-width oversized headline, a tall art tile, a working checklist, a small graphic tile and an indexed project tile. Mix spans and information density; do not repeat the same three-card hero used by other presets.

Typography: Bricolage Grotesque or a similarly expressive locally available sans, strong weight and tight display spacing. Keep body text and Korean fallback calm, legible and at least 1.6 line height.

Media: use an original abstract print with a circular pink form, black flowing wave and cream stripes. The shipped art is a style sample; choose subject-relevant original media for the actual project. Keep text and controls as real HTML.
Detail: 24px rounded modules, flat bold colour, generous internal padding and little shadow. A checkbox must change state; a project action must open relevant content.
Responsive: change three columns to two at medium widths; give the headline full width on small screens and keep small modules paired only while labels fit. Test 320px and desktop without clipping.
Motion: short tile hover or a single entrance sequence; respect reduced motion. Validate actual rendered colour balance, different tile proportions, keyboard controls and the selected tokens.

botanicalAtelier.label: Botanical Atelier
rules: Identity: an organic care brand with ivory paper, forest typography and olive accents. The botanical subject, sunlight and slower rhythm are central.

Composition: a generous serif headline beside a tall arched photograph, followed by three quiet product rituals separated by fine rules. Include one small botanical seal rather than decorating every surface.
Typography: DM Serif Display or a locally available organic serif; generous title scale, short italic accent and readable simple body type with Korean fallback.

Media: sunlit foliage, wildflowers, green glass and natural stone or linen. Crop with an arched top while preserving the product and enough plant context. Use original or licensed relevant photography.
Detail: restrained olive action, cream surfaces and thin botanical-green borders. Avoid medical claims or invented sustainability certifications in sample copy.
Responsive: stack copy then image; keep the arch tall and let ritual labels wrap naturally at 320px. Preserve whitespace without forcing empty full-screen sections.
Behaviour: ritual actions show usable product or routine information. Keep motion quiet and optional; verify image loading, keyboard focus, text contrast and mobile crop against the selected tokens.

clayPop.label: Clay Pop
rules: Identity: a friendly creative learning space with peach, lilac, cream and plum. Use soft dimensional objects and inflated surfaces rather than generic flat illustrations.

Composition: rounded heavy headline at left, one large lilac clay sculpture at right, followed by three course modules with different sculptural symbols. On task screens retain the same material language without forcing a marketing hero.
Typography: Bricolage Grotesque or a rounded expressive sans; strong friendly display weight, compact title lines and simple readable Korean body text.

Media: a tactile clay headphone or subject-relevant 3D object with visible surface texture, soft directional light and contact shadow. The real image must anchor the layout; avoid substituting a blank blob.
Material: peach background, cream inflated course surfaces, large 24-32px corners, subtle inner highlight and a grounded soft shadow. Use the confirmed tokens as the adjustable base.
Interaction: a raised main action has a visible focus state and opens course details; small hover motion may reinforce its volume without moving surrounding text.

Responsive: stack the sculpture below the headline and change course cards into compact horizontal rows on phones. Verify shape, image crop and 320px reading; disable decorative motion for reduced motion.

curatedEditorial.label: Architecture Editorial
rules: Identity: a considered editorial studio with warm gray canvas and near-black typography. The Awwwards reference means expressive, usable art direction, not a copied vendor website.

Composition: a monumental two-line heading beside a narrow introduction, a large unfiltered subject photograph, a ruled project index and a simple inquiry form. Do not substitute three statistic cards or geometric filler for the photographic focal point.
Typography: strong grotesk display scale, tight tracking and quiet UI text; preserve confirmed fonts and Korean legibility. Let mobile headlines wrap without cropping words.
Media: use original subject-relevant photography with a stable landscape crop. The included courtyard image belongs to the fictional FORM / FIELD sample and is not a real customer project.
Detail: sharp geometry, fine horizontal rules, generous margins and small project captions. Use the confirmed radius, spacing and color tokens if the user customizes them.

Interaction: project rows disclose actual information, navigation reaches relevant sections, and inquiry input has clear validation and feedback. Connect real submission only when requested; identify local previews truthfully.

Responsive: stack headline and introduction, retain the photograph as the focal point, and keep project titles and contact controls usable at 320px. Compare real rendered desktop and mobile screens against the chosen reference.

curatedKnowledge.label: Knowledge Workspace
rules: Identity: a quiet team knowledge workspace with true white document, off-white side rail and one understated blue accent. The Notion name is a style reference, not a copied identity.

Composition: searchable document navigation, breadcrumb, shallow photographic cover, readable document title and metadata, a concise callout, table of contents and a working checklist. Do not turn the document into a marketing hero or metrics dashboard.
Typography: constrain the document reading measure, use strong section hierarchy, and keep body copy and Korean fallback comfortable at normal sizes. Respect confirmed font and spacing tokens.
Media: use a calm original editorial cover with no overlaid UI text; preserve its crop while allowing user-provided subject matter to replace the sample vase photograph.

Interaction: document search has a clear empty state, selecting a document changes its real content and active navigation, and checkboxes update completion visibly. Use native controls and keyboard focus.
Data: fictional FIELDNOTES documents demonstrate the design. They must not be inserted as the user's actual team policies or meeting records.

Responsive: turn the sidebar into compact navigation, stack the table of contents below prose and keep checkboxes and related-document links reachable at 320px. Verify desktop and mobile rendering with the confirmed tokens.

curatedProduct.label: Product Workspace
rules: Identity: a focused dark productivity workspace, with off-black background, quiet dark surfaces and one muted periwinkle accent. The Linear name is a style reference, not an instruction to copy the product.

Composition: compact sidebar, project breadcrumb and heading, progress strip, category filters, three kanban columns and an inline task inspector. Build the actual workflow instead of a marketing hero with fake metrics.
Typography: readable system sans for controls, consistent label sizes, restrained headings and tabular details. Keep confirmed font and color tokens.
Detail: fine borders, modest radii, subtle elevation and compact status labels; reserve the accent for selected tasks and actionable controls.

Interaction: search and filters combine, tasks open an inspector, status edits move the task to the correct column, and task creation updates derived totals. Use native controls and visible keyboard focus.
Data: calculate progress from actual tasks. Sample records and fictional team members demonstrate layout only and must not become production project facts or falsely live data.
Responsive: collapse the sidebar to compact navigation and stack kanban columns when cards no longer fit. Test search, creation, status changes and empty states at desktop and 320px.

curatedSaas.label: Subscription Studio
rules: Identity: a refined subscription software site with cool white canvas, navy text, muted blue action and diffuse product-panel depth. Treat Stripe as a visual reference, not a copied identity.

Composition: expressive headline and concise product explanation beside one native billing dashboard, followed by a billing-period selector and two distinct horizontal pricing plans. Avoid decorative floating payment cards or repetitive feature tiles.
Typography: editorial serif display where the confirmed font allows it, with clear sans UI labels and calm price hierarchy. Preserve user-selected fonts and Korean fallback.

Product view: implement charts, subscription rows and labels as native accessible UI rather than a flattened screenshot. Label illustrative values as sample data and provide a readable chart description.
Pricing: monthly and yearly choices must update amounts and explain the billing period. Selecting a plan must provide truthful feedback and must not imply a real purchase when no checkout exists.
Tokens: maintain confirmed colors, radius and shadow; use appropriate readable foregrounds on primary buttons. Keep whitespace consistent between hero and pricing.
Responsive: stack hero copy and product panel, simplify the dashboard rail and place plans vertically on narrow screens. Verify price legibility, keyboard controls and 320px overflow.

cyberDeck.label: Cyber Deck
rules: Identity: an instrument-style science-fiction console with near-black, acid lime and restrained cyan. Use purposeful technical structure rather than random glowing ornaments.

Composition: a narrow status rail, dominant wireframe globe or relevant technical visualization, terminal pane and a thin signal strip. The visualization takes more space than the surrounding instruments.
Typography: local monospace, compact uppercase instrument labels and a large two-line status title. Keep important labels readable and avoid using illegible microtype for actual controls.

Artwork: use an original wire-globe image with CSS orbit animation, or render a relevant visualization in SVG or canvas. Separate decorative coordinates from real telemetry; label sample data and simulated status explicitly.
Detail: fine lime borders, dark solid panels, restrained glow and a high-contrast primary console action. A future HUD can use chamfered geometry while retaining accessible rectangular hit areas.

Responsive: reduce three instrument columns to two then one. Keep the visual large, wrap terminal lines and make each control at least 44px tall. Verify 320px and desktop without horizontal scrolling.

Behaviour: local sample diagnostics must never pretend to operate real infrastructure. Provide a visible pause for looping visualization and disable it with reduced motion; verify focus, readable results and selected tokens.

dataTool.label: Dense Data Tool
rules: Composition: use a compact page title and scoped summary, a search/filter/action toolbar, then a real table or operations list. Keep the main data within the first desktop viewport.
Hierarchy: page title at 1.75-2 times body size, table text at 0.875-1 times, labels at 0.8 times. Use tabular numbers, right-aligned amounts and stable column widths.
Density: target 44-52px rows with the confirmed padding token governing container spacing. Distinguish table headings, totals and selected rows using weight and surface contrast.
Content: show meaningful identifiers, names, states and timestamps. Use text labels as well as colors for warnings and completion; unavailable values must say so rather than becoming zero.
Controls: place filters together, display active filter count and a clear action, preserve selections while sorting, and explain empty/error states near the affected data.

Responsive: keep comparison tables in a labeled local horizontal scroller when columns must remain aligned; otherwise use stacked labeled rows. Never hide critical status or identifiers just to fit mobile.
Keep decorative heroes, product illustrations and unrelated metrics out of operational workflows. A precise grid and clear state hierarchy carry the visual identity.
Preserve confirmed tokens. Verify a populated view, no results, error, keyboard navigation and 320/390px layouts with real browser evidence.

editorialMotion.label: Editorial Motion
rules: Composition: a compact masthead, a 7:5 headline/visual split, then an indexed list of selected work. Use this structure for editorial or portfolio content; retain task-focused layouts for operational screens.

Hierarchy: one dominant headline at 3-4 times body size, section titles at 1.5 times, and quiet metadata at 0.8 times. Use short Korean lines, word-break: keep-all, and 1.2 heading / 1.7 body line heights.
Rhythm: use the confirmed spacing token as one unit; allow 2 units between sections and half a unit within related content. Align text and imagery to one grid instead of framing every block.
Focal point: use one relevant photograph, illustration, or designed typographic study. Preserve image aspect ratios; do not replace every image with an empty colored rectangle.
Details: pair project names with categories and small indices, use fine section rules, and reserve the primary fill for the main action. Use real content rather than invented popularity metrics.
Responsive: collapse the split into headline then visual below 700px; reduce display type to 2-2.75 times body size and move row metadata below titles. Prevent long Korean titles from clipping.
Motion: a single short reveal or restrained hover is sufficient; respect prefers-reduced-motion and keep reading/navigation immediately available.
Confirm tokens and references first. Verify hierarchy, image crop, row alignment, keyboard focus and 320/390px plus desktop layouts in the browser; fix differences before handoff.

industrialBrutalist.label: Industrial Brutalist
rules: Composition: create a strong masthead, a headline/graphic split for expressive pages, and an indexed production list. Operational screens begin with their controls and data instead of a decorative hero.
Hierarchy: bold display text at 3-4 times body size, section headings at 1.5 times, and monospaced identifiers at 0.8-0.875 times. Keep general Korean UI text on a readable sans stack.
Structure: use the confirmed border width and radius consistently, a disciplined grid, and one primary accent. Use the padding token as a section unit; align indices and names across rows.
Focal point: choose a strong typographic or geometric study tied to the subject. Contrast a large headline with compact metadata; keep body copy and control labels calm and readable.
Controls: use clear pressed, focused and disabled states. Hard shadows or physical translation are optional and must respect confirmed shadow/radius tokens and reduced-motion preferences.
Responsive: stack the split, reduce headline scale, wrap metadata under item names and retain usable 44px touch targets at 320px. Avoid forcing desktop grids to shrink below legible sizes.
Preserve user tokens and references. Inspect actual desktop/mobile renders for alignment, contrast, text wrapping and interaction feedback before handoff.

kineticType.label: Kinetic Type
rules: Identity: a bold culture studio in electric purple, warm white and acid yellow, led by expressive typography and controlled movement.
Composition: a compact italic wordmark above an oversized staggered LESS / ORDINARY. / MORE YOU. statement, a yellow action, a narrow moving type band and a white reversed project index.

Typography: a strong condensed italic display such as Anton with deliberate line-by-line sizing and offsets; Bricolage Grotesque or a similar expressive sans for support. Use native text, not a screenshot of lettering.
Artwork: the headline is the hero artwork. One large asterisk or typographic seal may balance the empty corner; do not substitute a stock photo or generic gradient blob.
Detail: dominant purple canvas, almost no rounded cards, thin dividers and an indexed work list. Keep only one clearly dominant action above the list.

Responsive: scale and offset each headline line inside the viewport, keep punctuation visible and wrap project metadata beneath names on narrow screens. Check both Korean replacement copy and the sample Latin display.

Motion: the type band loops slowly with a visible pause control; respect prefers-reduced-motion. Navigation and project details remain usable when static. Check actual text bounds, focus, contrast and selected tokens at 320px and desktop.

minimalistUtility.label: Minimalist Utility
rules: Composition: use a quiet navigation row, breadcrumb, a document-width reading column, title and summary, then ordered sections or notes. Keep supporting tools close to the content they affect.
Hierarchy: body at the confirmed base size with 1.7 line height, title at 2-2.75 times, subheadings at 1.25-1.5 times, and metadata at 0.8-0.875 times. Limit prose to about 60-72 characters per line.
Rhythm: use the confirmed padding token between sections and half that for connected rows. Structure lists with alignment and subtle rules; do not put every paragraph or metric in a separate card.
Details: use descriptive document names, dates, small indices and restrained icons. Give selected navigation, links and important actions a distinct emphasis without making all text bold.
Controls: keep search, editing and disclosure behavior explicit. Use native semantics and visible focus; expose useful empty, saved and error states where the user is working.
Responsive: collapse navigation to a compact menu and keep the reading column fluid with 16-24px side gutters. Wrap long names and move secondary metadata to a new line.
Preserve confirmed colors, radii, framework and existing font assets. Check reading comfort, text selection, keyboard actions and 320/390px plus desktop renders.

noirLuxe.label: Noir Luxe
rules: Identity: a fragrance or luxury editorial with near-black, warm ivory and champagne gold. Luxury comes from proportion, photography and typographic restraint, not glossy badges everywhere.

Composition: a fine-rule masthead, a large serif statement in the left half and a tall dramatic product photograph at right. A quiet three-note composition strip follows; no generic dashboard metrics.

Typography: Cormorant Garamond at light weight or an elegant local serif for display and a clean small sans or mono for labels. Allow short italic emphasis and broad whitespace; Korean titles use a compatible serif fallback.
Media: amber glass, dark stone, gold reflection and a directional spotlight. Keep the product sharply visible with intentional negative space and do not overlay paragraphs on busy highlights.
Detail: square edges, sparse hairlines, modest warm-gold actions and widely spaced small labels. Use genuine product attributes rather than invented ratings or scarcity.
Responsive: headline first, then a tall uncropped product image and readable scent notes. Preserve image focal point at 320px and desktop; avoid shrinking all text to fit the desktop layout.
Behaviour: collection action opens a relevant product story. Motion is a restrained reveal only; reduced motion remains static. Confirm contrast on the actual image and on all interactive states.

paperCollage.label: Paper Collage
rules: Identity: a personal editorial journal with blush paper, chocolate serif text and tangible analogue photographs. Preserve the warmth of collected objects.
Composition: a quiet masthead, left-aligned editorial title and overlapping photo prints on the right, followed by two issue entries on fine rules. Avoid a repeated grid of identical cards.
Typography: DM Serif Display or a compatible literary serif, generous readable body leading, small issue numbers and restrained handwritten accents only where legible.

Media: actual wildflower, architecture and coastline photographs arranged as rotated ivory prints with paper tape and soft natural shadows. The collage may be a dedicated image asset; headings, links and article content remain native HTML.

Detail: subtle paper grain, asymmetry contained within a clear reading grid and modest underlined or solid actions. Do not put large paragraphs over the photographs or flatten the whole page into a mockup image.
Responsive: move the photo collage below the introduction, then stack issue entries with a horizontal separator. Preserve image proportions and avoid rotated-photo overflow at 320px.
Behaviour: journal action opens a readable entry. Keep motion static or minimal, respect reduced motion and verify image loading, focus, contrast and the selected tokens on desktop and mobile.

premiumFrontend.label: Premium Frontend
rules: Composition: for a workspace use a compact navigation bar or 216-240px sidebar, a page heading with one primary action, a short summary strip, then the main project list. Marketing pages require their own story and visual hierarchy.

Hierarchy: use body text as the base, page title at 2-2.25 times base, section titles at 1.2 times, and metadata at 0.8-0.875 times. Keep Korean UI text on the sans stack; reserve monospace for identifiers and numbers.

Density: use the confirmed padding token for panels and half that spacing between related controls. Aim for 44px primary controls and 56-72px project rows with aligned name, owner, status and next action.
Surfaces: background establishes the workspace; a single surface layer groups content. Prefer dividers within lists, borders for interactive controls, and shadows only for floating layers.

Identity: select one content-led visual motif such as progress tracks, issue identifiers or compact thumbnails. Give the primary action enough contrast and use secondary buttons with lower visual weight.
States: implement selected navigation, hover, visible keyboard focus, loading, empty and error states with useful next actions. Never invent healthy operational statistics for production screens.
Responsive: move sidebar navigation to an accessible drawer on small screens; put actions below titles and project metadata below the main label. Preserve meaningful row order at 320px.
Preserve confirmed tokens and reference assets. Compare the actual browser result at 390px and desktop for type hierarchy, density, alignment, color contrast and working controls.

redesignGuard.label: Redesign Guard
rules: Start with the actual screen, its main task and working routes. Record the current information order and component states before changing appearance.

Establish a type hierarchy with one page title, clear section headings, body copy and quiet metadata. Use the existing font and confirmed size tokens as the base; fix inconsistent weights and line heights.
Consolidate spacing around one unit based on confirmed padding. Align labels, controls and content edges; remove redundant containers only when their grouping has no meaning.
Strengthen the primary action, selected state and focus visibility. Keep useful secondary actions discoverable and maintain empty, loading, error and disabled behavior.
Choose one identity detail from the product or confirmed reference; avoid applying an unrelated portfolio hero, generic metric cards or a different navigation model.
Preserve saved data, routes, component APIs, framework, colors and confirmed tokens. Explain any accessibility-related token conflict before changing a value.
Compare before/after screenshots at 320/390px and desktop. Check real content, long names, overflow, keyboard order and the unchanged primary workflow; scope final claims to evidence.

retroSunset.label: Retro Sunset
rules: Identity: a sunny analogue music poster in buttercream, burgundy and burnt orange. Use chunky retro lettering and recognisable record graphics.
Composition: a short oversized stacked title on the left, nested sunset arches and a large vinyl disc on the right, then a full-width event band and a flat lineup timetable.
Typography: Caprasimo or a comparably soft heavy retro serif for display, with plain sans timetable text. Preserve the character of the thick curved letters; a thin default serif loses this identity.
Artwork: concentric record grooves, an orange sun arch and a small contrasting centre label can be drawn with CSS or vector shapes. These are intentional poster graphics, not placeholder media.
Detail: warm printed colours, minimal shadow and rounded pill actions. Keep the timetable unboxed and aligned; do not add unrelated SaaS cards or fake attendee counts.
Responsive: place the record below the headline and move timetable metadata beneath each event name on phones. Keep the title complete at 320px; reduce artwork size before shrinking body text.
Behaviour: lineup actions expose event information. Optional record rotation must have a pause and reduced-motion fallback; a static record is sufficient. Respect confirmed tokens and check contrast.

softPremium.label: Soft Premium Interface
rules: Composition: for a consumer or product page use a quiet masthead, a 6:5 copy/image split, concise benefits, then a curated product or service list. For finance and admin work retain the data workflow and apply only the surface/type treatment.
Hierarchy: headline at 2.75-3.5 times body size with 1.2 line height, readable supporting copy at base size with 1.7 line height, and restrained metadata. Avoid using thin text for functional labels.
Rhythm: use generous section gaps at 2 times the confirmed padding token and compact groups at half a token. Let the visual and heading establish hierarchy rather than oversized empty cards.

Material: start with background and one surface layer. Use confirmed radii, fine borders, and a single subtle shadow style; translucent material must improve layer separation and preserve text contrast.
Visual: use relevant, well-cropped product or environment imagery. If assets are unavailable, make a deliberate illustration or type composition, and identify it as illustrative.
Actions: one prominent primary action with a readable foreground; secondary actions are quieter. Provide keyboard focus and legible disabled/error states; do not rely on pale color alone.
Responsive: stack heading, image, benefits and details in reading order below 700px. Maintain image proportions and 44px touch targets, and respect reduced motion.
Preserve confirmed tokens and font assets. Verify crops, spacing, contrast, long Korean text and mobile/desktop renders before completion.

swissPoster.label: Swiss Poster
rules: Identity: an international typography exhibition in saturated cobalt, warm ivory and a single vermilion disc. A strong grid and monumental condensed letters carry the design.
Composition: compact masthead; narrow date rail; oversized NEW above a wide PERSPECTIVES line; a partially cropped disc behind the title; then a ruled programme index.

Typography: Anton or another locally available condensed display face, with normal-width sans or mono for small metadata. Size each title line deliberately rather than uniformly scaling a generic heading.
Artwork: the simple vermilion circle is the intended abstract poster artwork. Keep it behind the typographic hierarchy and outside reading paths; it does not need stock photography.
Detail: square controls, fine aligned rules, generous blue negative space and large programme labels. Avoid rounded card grids and decorative shadows in this direction.

Responsive: retain the date rail when it fits, move explanatory text below the title and allow programme metadata to wrap onto a second line. Test at 320px and desktop, including long translated titles.
Behaviour: programme actions reveal session details with keyboard focus. Keep motion minimal; check title bounds, contrast, font loading and chosen tokens before declaring the design complete.
